biography.text: Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn Mūsā ibn Shākir was the eldest of the three brothers known collectively as the Banū Mūsā and active in ninth-century Baghdad. Specialist accounts attribute several astronomical writings to him, but this dossier addresses a bibliographic problem: records attach overlapping titles and content to different authors and textual descriptions, so individual work identities require collation.
gaps: Complete the individual biography from early sources and separate evidence for his scholarly, administrative, and political activity.

timeline.text: The two astronomical records discussed here are associated with ninth-century material. The consulted catalogues do not establish a composition date for either item, and surviving witness copy dates must not be treated as composition dates.
gaps: Inspect the manuscripts and colophons before assigning chronology.

fields.text: The ISMI record titled Ḥarakat al-aflāk names Muḥammad as author, lists Kitāb al-hayʾa and Kitāb ḥarakat al-falak al-ūlā as aliases, and describes an account of the Palmyra–Raqqa expedition to measure the Earth. It says the exact same passage also occurs in a more extensive anonymous Hayʾat al-aflāk attributed to Qusṭā ibn Lūqā, and cites George Saliba's 1994 article, p. 119, for that attribution. Separately, the BEA and Iranica describe Muḥammad's Kitāb ḥarakat al-falak al-ūlā / Book on the First Motion of the Celestial Sphere as a critique of Ptolemaic cosmology. The records may be related, but this batch does not establish whether they denote one work, overlapping recensions, or distinct texts. No cosmological passage has been directly read here.
gaps: Compare the Arabic texts in Damascus Asad Ẓāhiriyya 4489 and Oxford Selden A.11, including their title pages, incipits, and colophons.
Read Saliba 1994 and Ragep 1993 directly; trace their attribution statements and the reported shared expedition passage to the cited manuscripts.
Establish whether the ISMI aliases identify a single codex/text, a catalogue-level equivalence, or distinct compositions before describing the cosmological critique and geodetic account together.

legacy.text: The available reference literature associates Muḥammad with early astronomical writing and reports a critique of Ptolemaic cosmology. The catalogue overlap and attributed shared passage expose a textual-identity question, not proof of a particular author's influence or a settled work genealogy. This draft preserves that uncertainty rather than merging claims into a single confident narrative.
gaps: Trace reception only after identifying the text and its witnesses; no influence pathway is established in this batch.

investigations.title: The motion-of-the-spheres titles, the expedition passage, and Qusṭā's attribution
investigations.field: History of astronomy / textual bibliography and attribution
investigations.historicalProblem: Do the ISMI record Ḥarakat al-aflāk and the BEA/Iranica Book on the First Motion of the Celestial Sphere refer to one work, and how should their different content descriptions and the reported shared geodetic passage be interpreted?
investigations.historicalContext: Ninth-century astronomical works survive through layered manuscript and catalogue traditions. Similar titles and aliases can refer to different textual layers or be normalized together by catalogues; shared passages may indicate reuse, excerpting, or another textual relationship, none of which should be inferred without collation.
investigations.method: Compare the consulted ISMI work record with the separate BEA and Iranica descriptions, and record the exact source of the Qusṭā attribution (ISMI's citation to Saliba 1994, p. 119). Track each claim to its own bibliographic record and preserve unresolved title relationships.
investigations.observationsOrCalculations: ISMI lists two manuscript witnesses (Damascus Asad Ẓāhiriyya 4489; Oxford Bodleian Selden A.11) and reports that an expedition passage appears in a more extensive anonymous Hayʾat al-aflāk attributed to Qusṭā. No manuscript text or astronomical computation was reconstructed.
investigations.reportedResult: The source set supports at least two descriptions that must be kept analytically distinct: an ISMI record for Ḥarakat al-aflāk with geodetic-expedition content and BEA/Iranica reports of Muḥammad's Ptolemaic-cosmology critique under overlapping title forms. ISMI itself reports a shared passage with a Qusṭā-attributed text. Exact work identity, recension, and authorship remain unresolved until direct collation.
investigations.whatWasNew: This batch identifies a possible catalogue conflation and turns it into an explicit research question. It does not claim discovery of a new theory, proof of independent composition, or proof of Qusṭā's authorship.
investigations.limitations: ISMI witness records could not be opened; the Arabic manuscripts, Saliba 1994, and Ragep 1993 were not directly consulted. BEA and Iranica summarize rather than reproduce the cosmology text. The exact shared passage and the relationship among title forms remain unverified.
investigations.laterInfluence: Not assessed; no reception chain has been established for either textual layer.

openQuestions: Open and compare the Damascus Asad Ẓāhiriyya 4489 and Oxford Selden A.11 witness records and images; establish folio-level text, titles, incipits, and colophons.
Read George Saliba's 1994 article, especially pp. 115–141 and p. 119; identify the anonymous Hayʾat al-aflāk text, its evidence, and exact Qusṭā attribution argument.
Consult Ragep 1993, vol. 2, pp. 502–510, for its edition and translation of the expedition passage; compare it with both manuscripts and the passage in the Qusṭā-attributed text.
Determine whether the ISMI alias Kitāb ḥarakat al-falak al-ūlā conflates the expedition report with BEA/Iranica's Ptolemaic-cosmology critique, or whether one text contains both.
Only after that collation, revise the profile's title, content, attribution, and any relationship to the anonymous Hayʾat al-aflāk.
